gate: fine_detail_share, against min_fine. The ratio below is reported and not gated: an anti-goal critic read a max_ratio of 3.6 beside a measured 5.13 and an ok of true as a check contradicting itself, and they were right to. A pore adds to the gradient across the grain as much as along it, so anisotropy cannot see the difference between painted stripes and visible oak — five renders moved it from 5.76 to 5.13 while the surface changed completely.
how: mean absolute first difference inside 128 px tiles, column to column (across the grain) and row to row (along it), median over the tiles
why: a board with only rings on it is a comb. Vessels and rays are what happens along the grain, and without them the surface reads as stripes rather than as a cut through fibre.
